title: What happens when one is divided by seven?
description: One is divided by seven by long division, with every remainder written down. The remainders come round again, and so does a block of six digits. Keeko doubts that the digits stop after the first six.
teaching_notes: One idea: the remainders must come round again, and then the digits come round with them. Watch for children who stop after the first six digits.

source: Find 1 ÷ 7 by long division, listing every remainder.
video_script.why: The child has seen divisions where the same remainder comes back at once, and now meets one where a whole list of remainders comes round before the first one returns.
video_script.substitution: the book's own long division of one by seven, with every remainder written down
video_script.anchor: One divided by seven, by long division
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip stops after six digits and writes zero point one four two eight five seven. Seven times that is only zero point nine nine nine nine nine nine, which is less than one.
video_script.payoff_line: The digits one four two eight five seven come round for ever.

final_answer.spoken: zero point one four two eight five seven, and the block one four two eight five seven repeats for ever

maths_rules: 1 is too small to share by 7, so 0 Ones; 1 One = 10 Tenths
50 ÷ 7: 7 × 7 = 49 and 50 − 49 = 1, so digit 7, remainder 1, where we started
the slip: 7 × 0.142857 = 0.999999, which is less than 1
video_script.design: One idea: a remainder smaller than seven must come round again, and the digits come round with it. Assumes long division with a decimal quotient. Wrong idea: stopping after the first six digits. The division stays all video; the working builds step by step; the quotient appears only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>When we share among seven, each box gets the same amount.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>What cannot be shared equally is left over, and it is always smaller than seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The leftover can only be one, two, three, four, five or six.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the number to be divided is one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The number we divide by is seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: 1 ÷ 7 by long division, with every remainder listed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find every digit and every remainder, and see when they begin again.

beats.on_screen: 1 is too small to share by 7, so 0 Ones; 1 One = 10 Tenths; 10 ÷ 7: 7 × 1 = 7; 10 − 7 = 3; digit 1, remainder 3

marks.m1: a zero is written in the ones place
marks.m2: the one is changed into ten tenths, and seven times one is written as seven
marks.m3: ten take away seven leaves three, and the digit and the remainder are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, one is too small to share by seven, so the ones digit is zero.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Change the one into ten tenths. Seven times one is seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Ten take away seven leaves three. The first digit is one, and the remainder is three.

marks.m1: the three is changed into thirty, and seven times four is written as twenty eight
marks.m2: thirty take away twenty eight leaves two
marks.m3: the two is changed into twenty, and seven times two is written as fourteen
marks.m4: twenty take away fourteen leaves six

beats.colours: the remainders in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, change the three into thirty. Seven times four is twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirty take away twenty eight leaves two. The digit is four, and the remainder is two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Change the two into twenty. Seven times two is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Twenty take away fourteen leaves six. The digit is two, and the remainder is six.

marks.m1: the six is changed into sixty, and seven times eight is written as fifty six
marks.m2: the four is changed into forty, and seven times five is written as thirty five
marks.m3: the five is changed into fifty, and seven times seven is written as forty nine

beats.colours: the remainders in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, change the six into sixty. Seven times eight is fifty six, and sixty take away fifty six leaves four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Change the four into forty. Seven times five is thirty five, and forty take away thirty five leaves five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Change the five into fifty. Seven times seven is forty nine, and fifty take away forty nine leaves one.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, list the remainders in order: one, three, two, six, four, five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The next remainder is one again, and that is where we started.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>From here the same remainders come again, and the same digits come with them, for ever.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>One divided by seven is zero point one four two eight five seven.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks it ends after six digits, with zero point one four two eight five seven.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But seven times that is only zero point nine nine nine nine nine nine. That is not one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The remainder after the last digit is one, not zero, so the digits start again.
